description: The code reviewer and the database reviewer both independently flag the SAME N+1 query problem, from their own reviewing angle, each as a P1. It is one real defect, not two.

findings.title: N+1 query when loading review findings
findings.description: `getReviewsForRepository` loops over every `Review` and calls `getFindingsForReviewerRun` inside the loop, issuing one query per reviewer run instead of a single batched query. For a repository with hundreds of reviews this multiplies request latency severely.
findings.recommendation: Batch-load all findings for the page of reviews in one query, keyed by reviewer run id.

findings.title: Per-row query pattern in getReviewsForRepository
findings.description: The loop in `getReviewsForRepository` (src/server/reviews/repository.ts) issues one `findings` query per reviewer run rather than a single `IN (...)` query. This is the same N+1 access pattern flagged from the query-shape side.
findings.recommendation: Replace the per-row query with a single batched query using `IN`.

reviewer_runs.summary: No architectural concerns beyond the query pattern already flagged.
Coverage is adequate for the change as written.

expected.rationale: Two reviewers describe the identical N+1 query defect at the identical file/line from two angles. Correctly recognized as ONE confirmed P1 root cause, the outcome matches the single-P1 floor: APPROVE_WITH_MINOR_FIXES. Treating it as two independent confirmed high-priority issues (double-counting) would overstate the real risk and could push the verdict stricter than the evidence actually supports.

explanation: Directly tests duplicate-risk inflation: a judge that treats these as two separate confirmed P1s (rather than one shared root cause) is at real risk of escalating to DO_NOT_APPROVE on double-counted evidence, and unlike the deterministic floor's own blind spot here (it also can't dedupe), nothing downstream would catch the judge doing this, since applyVerdictFloor only ever makes a verdict stricter, never overrides an already-stricter judge call.
